source.dirtyPolicy: not applicable; the script archives the committed HEAD via `git archive`, so uncommitted changes never ship (a dirty workspace only triggers a warning)

operations.name: deploy:init
preconditions: reachable SSH host with the dedicated WSL key
guard absent or identical to {targetId: ad, phase: production, lifecycleRevision: 1}
proof: remote guard file equals target ad, production, lifecycle revision 1 (read and compared before any mutation)
recovery: remove the non-secret guard file only before any release uses lifecycle revision 1

operations.name: deploy:code
preconditions: exclusive target lock (mkdir-based, fails immediately if held)
~/www/webpool.env present on the target (target-authoritative, never transferred, outside the swapped ~/www/webpool)
git archive of the commit plus `pnpm install --prod --frozen-lockfile` succeed in a native Linux WSL staging directory (not DrvFs)
proof: find over ~/www/webpool.new reports no directory other than 755 and no file other than 644
`webpool stats` exits 0 from ~/www/webpool.new before the swap
after the swap, ~/www/webpool/.env is a symlink to ~/www/webpool.env, ~/www/webpool/.htaccess denies all web access and ~/www/webpool/bin/webpool.js exists
recovery: swap ~/www/webpool.old back over ~/www/webpool; ~/www/webpool.old is only purged at the START of the next deploy:code, so it survives until then

sync.deletions: mirror code only; /.env and /.htaccess are excluded and written by the script

operations.name: deploy:schema
preconditions: fresh pg_dump -Fc of the database succeeds before migrating
proof: `webpool migrate` exits 0 (each migration runs in its own transaction with its schema_migration row)
`webpool stats` exits 0 against the migrated schema
recovery: pg_restore --clean --if-exists from ~/deploy/webpool-ad/backups/webpool-<stamp>-<commit>.dump; the five most recent dumps are kept
